en: opening a shop; starting a business

examples.ko: 이 가게는 오전 열 시에 개점해요.
examples.en: This shop opens at ten in the morning.
On opening day there is a discount event.

examples.ko: 개점 시간보다 일찍 가면 문이 닫혀 있어요.
examples.en: If you go before opening time, the door is closed.

examples.ko: 개점한 지 얼마 안 돼서 손님이 적어요.
examples.en: It hasn't been open long, so there are few customers.
We cleaned the shop ahead of the opening.

examples.ko: 그 식당은 올해 개점 오 주년이에요.
examples.en: That restaurant marks its fifth anniversary this year.

explain: 가게를 처음 여는 것뿐 아니라 그날 영업을 시작하는 것에도 써요. 영업을 끝내는 것은 '폐점', 영업을 쉬는 것은 '휴점'이라고 해요. 일상에서는 '문을 열다'나 '오픈하다'를 더 많이 말해요.

phrases.en: What time does the shop open?
phrases.nuance_ko: 그날 영업을 시작하는 시간을 물을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it to ask when business starts for the day.

phrases.example: 개점 기념 행사로 커피를 무료로 줘요.
phrases.en: They give out free coffee as an opening-day event.
phrases.nuance_ko: 새 가게가 열 때 하는 행사를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: It refers to an event held when a new shop opens.

phrases.example: 그 빵집은 아침 일곱 시에 문을 열어요.
phrases.en: That bakery opens at seven in the morning.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상에서는 '개점하다'보다 이 말을 더 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: In daily life this is used more than 개점하다.

explain_en: It covers both a shop's first opening and starting business for the day. Closing is '폐점' and taking time off is '휴점'. In daily talk people more often say '문을 열다' or '오픈하다'.

examples.ko: 낡은 벽보 위에 새 안내문이 겹겹이 붙어 있었어요.
examples.en: New notices were stuck in layers over the old posters.

examples.ko: 날씨가 너무 추워서 옷을 겹겹이 입었어요.
examples.en: It was so cold that I wore layer upon layer of clothes.
People surrounded the singer in rings, one behind another.

examples.ko: 산이 겹겹이 이어져 있어서 경치가 멋있어요.
examples.en: The mountains stretch ridge after ridge, so the view is wonderful.

examples.ko: 선물을 겹겹이 포장해서 무슨 물건인지 몰랐어요.
examples.en: The gift was wrapped in so many layers that I couldn't tell what it was.
Even when you peel an onion, more layers keep coming.

explain: 옷, 종이, 산, 사람처럼 여러 겹이 쌓이거나 둘러싼 모양에 써요. '겹겹이 쌓이다', '겹겹이 둘러싸다', '겹겹이 입다'처럼 같이 쓰는 말이 거의 정해져 있어요. 한 겹이 아니라 여러 겹이라는 걸 강조하고 싶을 때 좋아요.

phrases.en: Dust has piled up in layers in the storage room.
phrases.nuance_ko: 여러 겹으로 차곡차곡 쌓인 모양을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes things stacked up in many layers.

phrases.en: The police surrounded the building in several rings.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람이나 물건이 여러 겹으로 주변을 에워싼 모습이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Shows people or things forming several rings around a place.

phrases.en: I wrapped the dishes in many layers so they wouldn't break.
phrases.nuance_ko: 포장할 때 여러 겹으로 감싸는 것을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for wrapping something in many layers when packing.

explain_en: It describes things stacked or surrounding in many layers, such as clothes, paper, mountains or people. It is used in set combinations like '겹겹이 쌓이다', '겹겹이 둘러싸다' and '겹겹이 입다'. It is good for stressing that there are many layers, not just one.

examples.en: He has an easygoing personality and holds no grudges.

examples.ko: 저 사람은 뒤끝이 길어서 싸우면 오래 가요.
examples.en: That person holds grudges for a long time, so fights drag on.
My friend holds grudges, so I have to watch what I say.

examples.ko: 싸우고 나서도 뒤끝 없이 바로 풀었어요.
examples.en: Even after the fight, we made up right away without any lingering bad feelings.

examples.ko: 회의에서 크게 다퉜지만 뒤끝은 남기지 않기로 했어요.
examples.en: We argued a lot in the meeting, but we decided not to leave any bad feelings behind.

examples.ko: 뒤끝이 있는 성격이라 작은 일도 잊지 않아요.
examples.en: I tend to hold grudges, so I don't forget even small things.

explain: 사람의 성격을 말할 때 '뒤끝이 있다/없다/길다'라고 해요. '뒤끝이 없다'는 화를 내도 금방 풀고 마음에 담아 두지 않는다는 칭찬이에요. 반대로 '뒤끝이 있다'는 지난 일을 오래 기억하며 섭섭해한다는 뜻이라 조금 부정적이에요.

phrases.example: 그 친구는 뒤끝이 있어서 말조심해야 해요.
phrases.en: That friend holds grudges, so I have to watch my words.
phrases.nuance_ko: 싸운 일을 오래 마음에 담아 둔다는 뜻이라 조금 부정적이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means someone keeps a fight in mind for a long time, so it's a bit negative.

phrases.example: 우리 팀장님은 화를 내도 금방 풀리는 뒤끝 없는 사람이에요.
phrases.en: Our team leader gets angry but gets over it quickly; he holds no grudges.
phrases.nuance_ko: '뒤끝이 없다'를 사람을 꾸미는 말로 바꾼 칭찬이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A compliment that turns 뒤끝이 없다 into a phrase describing a person.

phrases.example: 동생은 뒤끝이 길어서 사과해도 오래 말을 안 해요.
phrases.en: My younger sibling holds grudges for a long time, so even after I apologize, they don't talk to me for a while.
phrases.nuance_ko: 섭섭한 마음이 오래 간다는 뜻으로, '뒤끝이 있다'보다 정도가 더 강해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means hurt feelings last a long time; stronger than 뒤끝이 있다.

explain_en: When describing personality, people say '뒤끝이 있다/없다/길다'. '뒤끝이 없다' is a compliment: someone gets over anger quickly and doesn't keep it inside. '뒤끝이 있다' is slightly negative, meaning the person remembers past offenses and stays upset.

examples.en: He shook his head with a wry smile.
All I could manage was a bitter smile at the news of failure.
It was so absurd that a wry smile came out.
I gave a forced smile at my friend's joke.
A faint bitter smile spread across his face.
Sadness was hidden behind the wry smile.

explain: 기쁘지 않거나 어이없을 때 억지로 짓는 웃음이에요. '쓴웃음을 짓다', '쓴웃음이 나다'처럼 자주 말해요. 맛이 쓰다는 뜻이 아니라 마음이 개운하지 않은 웃음이에요.

phrases.en: I gave a wry smile at my friend's joke.
phrases.nuance_ko: 쓴웃음이 나오는 것보다 일부러 표정을 만드는 느낌이 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: This stresses deliberately making the wry smile, rather than it just coming out.

phrases.en: My own mistake was so silly that I had to smile wryly.
phrases.nuance_ko: 자기도 모르게 웃음이 나오는 상황에 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use this when the wry smile comes out on its own.

phrases.en: He had a bitter smile on his face.
phrases.nuance_ko: 웃음이 얼굴에 남아 있는 모습을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use this to describe a smile that stays on someone's face.

explain_en: It is a smile you force when you are not happy or find something absurd. It is often said as '쓴웃음을 짓다' or '쓴웃음이 나다'. It has nothing to do with taste, but with a smile that leaves a sour feeling.

en: to be gentle; to be well-behaved

examples.en: My younger brother is well-behaved in front of strangers.
Our cat was calm at the vet.
The child sits quietly and reads a book.

examples.ko: 얌전한 줄 알았는데 말하면 재미있는 사람이에요.
examples.en: I thought he was quiet, but he is fun once he talks.
You should behave yourself during class.
That puppy is well-behaved, so it is easy to raise.

explain: '조용하다'는 소리가 없다는 뜻이고 '얌전하다'는 행동이 차분하고 말썽을 안 부리는 거예요. 아이나 동물에게 칭찬으로 많이 써요. 어른에게 쓰면 조금 답답한 느낌이 날 때도 있어요.

phrases.en: The kid next door is really well-behaved.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사를 꾸미는 활용이에요. 아이를 칭찬할 때 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A modifier form for nouns. Often used to praise a child.

phrases.en: I sit quietly and behave during class.
phrases.nuance_ko: '얌전하게'보다 '얌전히'가 더 자주 쓰이는 부사예요.
phrases.nuance_en: The adverb 얌전히 is used more often than 얌전하게.

phrases.en: Our puppy isn't very well-behaved.
phrases.nuance_ko: 부정형이에요. 말썽을 부리고 가만히 있지 않을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The negative form, used for someone who misbehaves and can't stay still.

explain_en: 조용하다 is about lack of noise, while 얌전하다 is about calm behavior without making trouble. It is a common compliment for kids and animals, though for adults it can sometimes sound a bit stuffy.

examples.en: I have never seen a sunset this beautiful.
Why did you get up this early?

examples.ko: 그 사람이 이토록 화를 낼 줄 몰랐어요.
examples.en: I did not know he would get this angry.
I have waited this long and still no one is coming.

examples.ko: 이토록 좋은 날씨에 집에만 있기 아까워요.
examples.en: It feels like a waste to stay home in weather this nice.

examples.ko: 이토록 많은 사람이 올 줄은 몰랐어요.
examples.en: I did not expect this many people to come.

explain: 일상 대화에서는 '이렇게'를 더 많이 써요. '이토록'은 놀람이나 아쉬움 같은 감정이 담긴 글, 노래 가사, 소설에서 자주 보여요. 정도를 강조하는 말이라 뒤에 '아름다운', '오래'처럼 정도를 나타내는 말이 자주 와요.

phrases.en: Why are you this late?
phrases.nuance_ko: '이토록'과 뜻이 같지만 일상 대화에서 훨씬 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as '이토록', but much more common in daily talk.

phrases.en: I didn't know it would be this hard.
phrases.nuance_ko: 예상보다 정도가 커서 놀랐을 때 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when something is far beyond what you expected.
phrases.en_equiv: didn't know it would be this much

phrases.en: This is the first time I've waited this long.
phrases.nuance_ko: 기다린 시간이 길어서 느끼는 감정을 강조해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Emphasizes the feeling about how long the wait was.

explain_en: In everyday talk Koreans say '이렇게' much more often. '이토록' appears in writing, song lyrics, and novels, where it carries feelings such as surprise or regret. It emphasizes degree, so it is often followed by words of degree like '아름다운' or '오래'.

examples.en: My older brother finishes his military service next month.
He was discharged two years ago.
After I am discharged, I will go back to school.
On the day he was discharged, his family came to meet him.
He got a job right after being discharged.
I am counting the days until I am discharged.

explain: 군대를 마치고 나올 때 쓰는 말이고 '입대하다'와 짝이에요. 일상에서는 '제대'를 많이 쓰고, 공식 서류에서는 '전역'을 써요. '군대 갔다 오다'도 같은 상황에서 자주 말해요.

phrases.example: 제대 후에 친구와 여행을 갈 거예요.
phrases.en: After I get discharged, I'm going to travel with a friend.
phrases.nuance_ko: 군대를 마친 뒤의 계획을 말할 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used when talking about plans after finishing military service.

phrases.en: My brother went to the army and came back last year.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상에서 제대했다는 뜻을 부드럽게 돌려 말하는 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A casual, softer way of saying someone has completed military service.

phrases.en: He was discharged from the military last year.
phrases.nuance_ko: 공식 서류나 정중한 자리에서 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The word used in official documents and formal situations.

explain_en: It is used when leaving the military and pairs with '입대하다' (enlist). In daily talk people say 제대, while official papers use '전역'. '군대 갔다 오다' is also common for the same situation.

examples.en: The witness testified in court exactly as he saw it.

examples.ko: 저는 그날 있었던 일을 증언할 수 있어요.
examples.en: I can testify to what happened that day.

examples.ko: 증인이 자신 있게 증언하는 모습을 봤어요.
examples.en: I saw the witness testify with confidence.

examples.ko: 친구가 제 편에서 증언해 줘서 오해가 풀렸어요.
examples.en: My friend spoke up on my side, and the misunderstanding was cleared.
It will help if you testify truthfully.
The victim gathered courage and decided to testify.

explain: '말하다'는 어디서나 쓰지만 '증언하다'는 재판이나 조사에서 내가 보고 들은 사실을 밝힐 때만 써요. 이 일을 하는 사람은 '증인', 말한 내용은 '증언'이에요. 거짓말을 하면 '위증'이 돼서 무거운 말이에요.

phrases.en: That person gave testimony in court.
phrases.nuance_ko: '증언하다'를 명사 '증언'으로 바꿔 쓴 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The verb turned into the noun 증언.

phrases.example: 그 사건의 증인이 오늘 법원에 와요.
phrases.en: The witness in that case comes to court today.
phrases.nuance_ko: 증언하는 사람을 부르는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The word for the person who testifies.

phrases.en: Tomorrow I am going to court to testify.
phrases.nuance_ko: 증언하려고 어디에 간다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say you are going somewhere in order to testify.

explain_en: '말하다' works anywhere, but '증언하다' is only for stating what you saw or heard in a trial or investigation. The person is a '증인' and what they say is '증언'. Lying there is '위증', so it is a heavy word.

examples.en: The army charged into the enemy's castle.

examples.ko: 화가 난 손님이 가게 안으로 쳐들어가서 소리쳤어요.
examples.en: An angry customer barged into the shop and shouted.
Our team decided to charge into the enemy camp.

examples.ko: 아이들이 형 방으로 쳐들어가 장난을 쳤어요.
examples.en: The kids burst into their older brother's room and played pranks.

examples.ko: 경찰이 가게로 쳐들어가는 장면이 영화에 나와요.
examples.en: There's a scene in the movie where the police storm into a shop.

examples.ko: 게임에서 상대 기지로 쳐들어가야 이길 수 있어요.
examples.en: In the game you can only win by attacking the opponent's base.

explain: 그냥 '들어가다'와 달리 힘차게, 공격하듯이 안으로 들어가는 느낌이에요. 전쟁이나 게임뿐 아니라 화가 난 사람이 갑자기 들어갈 때도 써요. 반대로 들어오는 쪽에서 말하면 '쳐들어오다'예요.

phrases.example: 경찰이 문을 열고 쳐들어가서 범인을 잡았어요.
phrases.en: The police burst in and caught the criminal.
phrases.nuance_ko: 연결형이라서 뒤에 이어지는 행동을 같이 말할 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: A connective form that lets you add the next action.

phrases.en: The soldiers attacked the enemy camp at night.
phrases.nuance_ko: 전쟁이나 게임 이야기에서 자주 나오는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common pairing in war or game contexts.

phrases.example: 화가 나도 남의 집에 쳐들어가지 마세요.
phrases.en: Even if you're angry, don't barge into someone's house.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명령이나 부탁을 할 때 쓰는 말투로, 화가 나서 들어가는 상황에 어울려요.
phrases.nuance_en: A request or command form, fitting angry intrusions.

explain_en: Unlike plain '들어가다', it feels like entering forcefully, like an attack. It is used for war and games, and also when an angry person bursts in. When seen from the side being entered, the word is '쳐들어오다'.

en: to withdraw; to drop; to call off

examples.en: He withdrew the lawsuit.
To withdraw the report, you must go to the police station.

examples.ko: 두 사람이 화해해서 고소를 취하하기로 했어요.
examples.en: The two made up and decided to drop the complaint.

examples.ko: 신청서를 취하한 사람은 다시 낼 수 있어요.
examples.en: A person who withdrew an application can submit it again.
The lawyer advised withdrawing the request.
The company withdrew its patent application.

explain: 주로 소송, 고소, 신청 같은 법이나 서류와 관련된 일에 쓰는 딱딱한 말이에요. 일상에서 약속이나 주문을 없앨 때는 '취소하다'를 써요. '취하'와 '취소'는 비슷하지만 '취하'는 내가 낸 것을 거두는 느낌이 강해요.

phrases.en: He decided to drop the complaint.
phrases.nuance_ko: 경찰이나 법원에 낸 고소를 거두는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means withdrawing a complaint filed with the police or court.

phrases.en: The documents were wrong, so I withdrew my application.
phrases.nuance_ko: 내가 낸 신청을 거둘 때 써요. 일상에서는 '취소하다'가 더 흔해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to withdraw your own application. In daily talk '취소하다' is more common.

phrases.en: You can still withdraw the lawsuit now.
phrases.nuance_ko: 취하가 가능한지 물을 때나 알려 줄 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to ask or tell whether withdrawal is possible.

explain_en: This is a formal word used for legal or paperwork matters such as lawsuits, complaints and applications. For canceling plans or orders in daily life, use 취소하다. 취하하다 leans toward taking back something you yourself filed.

dis.h: withdraw a lawsuit or formal filing

p.n: 철회하다 also works for a lawsuit but is broader; 취하하다 is mainly for legal and formal filings.

en: to regret; to feel remorse; to repent

examples.en: I regret not saying it back then.
I bought expensive shoes and regretted it right away.
Do your best so you won't regret it.
There is nothing I regret.
I bought it because I thought I'd regret it later.
If you regret it, you can just start again.

explain: '후회하다'는 내가 의식적으로 후회할 때, '후회되다'는 마음이 저절로 그렇게 될 때 써요. '~ㄴ 게 후회돼요' 형태로 자주 말해요. 명사 '후회'는 '후회가 돼요'처럼 써요.

phrases.example: 말을 심하게 한 게 후회가 돼요.
phrases.en: I regret that I spoke so harshly.
phrases.nuance_ko: '후회되다'와 뜻이 같고, 명사 '후회'를 써서 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as 후회되다 but built with the noun 후회.

phrases.en: Don't regret it later.
phrases.nuance_ko: '후회하다'는 스스로 하는 일이라서 명령이나 부탁에도 쓸 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: 후회하다 is something a person does, so it works in commands and requests.

phrases.en: I don't regret this choice at all.
phrases.nuance_ko: 후회하는 마음이 없다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say that you have no feeling of regret.

explain_en: '후회하다' is the act of regretting; '후회되다' is when the feeling arises by itself. A common form is '~ㄴ 게 후회돼요'. With the noun you can say '후회가 돼요'.

examples.en: The yard has a dirt floor, so it gets muddy when it rains.
The kids sit on the dirt ground and play marbles.

examples.ko: 이 가게는 바닥이 시멘트가 아니라 흙바닥이에요.
examples.en: The floor of this shop is dirt, not cement.
I spread a mat over the dirt ground and sat down.
The dirt surface of the schoolyard is wet from rain and slippery.
Walking barefoot on the dirt ground felt new.

explain: 포장하지 않고 흙 그대로인 바닥을 말해요. 반대 느낌의 말은 '시멘트 바닥', '콘크리트 바닥'이에요. 비슷한 '맨땅'은 풀도 깔개도 없는 땅 자체를 말할 때 써요.

phrases.en: The children sit on the dirt ground and play.
phrases.nuance_ko: 포장되지 않은 바닥에 앉을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when sitting on unpaved ground.
phrases.en_equiv: to sit on the dirt ground

phrases.en: The inside of the market is still a dirt floor.
phrases.nuance_ko: 바닥이 흙 그대로라고 설명할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to describe that the floor is bare earth.

phrases.en: If you sit on bare ground, your clothes get dirty.
phrases.nuance_ko: 풀이나 깔개가 없는 땅 자체를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to bare ground with no grass or covering.

explain_en: It means a floor or ground left as bare soil, not paved. The opposite feel is '시멘트 바닥' or '콘크리트 바닥'. The similar '맨땅' is used for the bare ground itself with no grass or covering.
